composition_notes: Keeps the expedition-and-beacon setting central, uses five participants without naming an answer, and foregrounds the six required relational evidence dimensions. The concept is defined exactly as requested while avoiding genre-mystery framing, role-based shortcuts, and an answer reveal in the opening.
intended_answer: Determine the participant whose relational, temporal, causal, spatial, sequence, and protocol evidence statuses yield the accepted iterated modular checksum. No participant is selected or implied in the premise.
premise: During a desert expedition, five survey participants recover a chain of emergency beacons buried along an abandoned salt-road route. Each beacon contains damaged fragments that must be decoded in order, while the team’s field logs, radio timestamps, route markers, equipment records, and handoff notes preserve conflicting clues about who interacted with which signal and when. The expedition’s local rulebook classifies each participant’s evidence as relational, temporal, causal, spatial, sequence, or protocol status, then combines the six statuses through an accepted iterated modular checksum. The locally defined target concept, “coherent signal bearer,” is the one participant whose six evidence statuses produce the incident’s accepted iterated modular checksum under those local rules. The crew must establish that bearer from the complete evidence chain rather than from rank, equipment ownership, or narrative prominence.
setting_summary: A desert expedition decoding a chain of emergency beacons across an abandoned salt-road corridor, using field records and recovered signal fragments to reconcile a complicated incident.
target_question: Which participant is the coherent signal bearer under the local evidence-status rules and accepted iterated modular checksum?
